description: An autonomous company working 24/7 on your own PC - Windows/Linux/macOS.

summary.one_liner: A Python framework that runs a continuous loop of AI CLI calls (Claude Code or Codex CLI) where 14 expert-persona agent roles plan, build, and operate a virtual company on your own PC.
summary.what_it_does: The project runs a loop (scripts/core/auto-loop.sh) that repeatedly calls an LLM CLI, by default Claude Code, with Codex CLI also supported. Each cycle reads a shared work summary in memories/consensus.md and a per-cycle prompt, then the agent decides what to do, may form a team of 2-5 of the 14 role definitions in .claude/agents/, and updates the summary before the next cycle. The 14 roles (CEO, CTO, QA, Marketing, CFO and others) are persona prompts modeled on named industry figures. The repo also includes 30+ reusable skills in .claude/skills/. A local dashboard shows cycle reports, status, usage, budgets, and logs, and a Product Center catalogs connected product runs. Failure handling includes rate-limit waits, a circuit breaker after consecutive errors, and consensus rollback. Daemon mode uses launchd on macOS and systemd --user inside WSL on Windows.
use_cases: run an autonomous AI team on a personal computer
automate product research and idea validation
continuous coding loop with Claude Code or Codex
monitor AI agent cycles and usage budgets via a local dashboard
steer a long-running agent by editing a markdown summary
generate small apps and landing pages unattended
how_to_run: make start  (foreground run, default engine Claude Code)
ENGINE=codex make start  (use Codex CLI instead)
make install  (install background daemon on macOS or WSL)
make pause / make resume  (pause or resume daemon)
notable: 14 expert-persona agent roles (e.g., Bezos, Munger, DHH) defined as prompts in .claude/agents/
Daemon auto-restart via launchd on macOS and systemd --user in WSL
Local dashboard with cycle reports, usage, budgets and logs; Product Center for connecting and browsing product runs
File-based steering: edit memories/consensus.md between runs to change direction
Configurable via environment variables for engine, model, loop interval, timeout and circuit-breaker threshold
caveats: Experimental project; stability not guaranteed, per the README
Each cycle consumes model quota, so it costs money
Default engine settings allow broad local actions (bypassPermissions); no OS-level sandbox, and prompt rules are not enforced isolation
Windows requires WSL2 (Ubuntu); PowerShell is only the control layer
Deployment and marketing depend on available tools and authorization; no guarantee a product is completed or deployed
